trust_decision.summary: Diagram-author-controlled service/junction/group IDs are used as plain-object keys in the ArchitectureDB lookup tables; the DB decides whether an ID names a real group (inherited keys such as __proto__ pass the existence check), and getDataStructures then writes the group-alignment table keyed by those IDs, so a parent of __proto__ writes onto Object.prototype.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'Architecture diagrams ... prototype pollution'. The only nested-object write keyed by user IDs is the groupAlignments ??= {} / [a][b] = alignment block in the DB.

diagram DB validation (parent existence check uses inherited keys)

fix_sites.module_kind: data-structure builder (adjacency list, BFS spatial map, group alignment table) - the sink

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The renderer only reads groupAlignments and builds local per-render objects; once the DB stops polluting, a solver can argue the renderer is 'just layout' and leave it. But then a legitimate __proto__ group (which the fix must allow) breaks at the ??= [] / push in the renderer, and a changed table shape breaks the read at :189.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: '__proto__' (and other inherited names such as toString/constructor) must stay valid group/service IDs: the fix test requires 'group __proto__' to parse and appear in getGroups(). Today addGroup rejects it as 'already in use'. A fix that just denies those IDs breaks this. Services must also keep their declaration order, including numeric IDs (fix.diff:76-84).

legitimately declared group named __proto__ whose ID then keys the alignment table
group IDs on either side of a cross-group edge (lhs and rhs both written)
service vs junction vs group parent (three add* routes)
edge endpoints / align members naming inherited keys (addEdge, addLayoutHint)
IDs containing '-' (fix key uses JSON.stringify per ID so the pair key is unambiguous; ID terminal allows '-' per packages/parser/src/language/common/common.langium:27)

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: svgDraw already caches elements per ID through the DB; a maintainer adding group-nesting padding would naturally write cache[groupId] ??= {} in the drawing code

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a declared-pair lookup moved to a nested object (pairs[a][b] = true) or a '-'-joined string key
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the layout-hint code already builds pair keys by string joining; a nested-object variant or '-' separator (IDs may contain '-') is an equally natural implementation and makes a how-type identity/separator sibling

O8b_injection_room.sibling: keep the renderer's per-row/per-group objects and add a group-to-group alignment override table keyed by user group IDs
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the align directive feature (layoutHints) is recent and is an obvious place to extend with group-level alignment

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject __proto__/constructor/prototype IDs in the parser or add*, or guard only groupAlignments[...] with hasOwn. This breaks the required '__proto__ as group name' behaviour, and the renderer and existence checks keep using inherited-key lookups.
